name: Baseline 4PS (Lighthouse Health & Wellness)
why: Free wellness app built only for public safety (law enforcement, fire, EMS, corrections, dispatch) that passively syncs sleep, HRV and resting heart rate from a connected wearable and builds personal baselines; App Store listing names Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop 'and more'. Lighthouse is a public benefit corporation owned by public safety agencies, is FirstNet Verified, and is listed as an FOP wellness provider.
why_now: Baseline 4PS is a new App Store listing (id6761061898); no launch date published.
opportunity: Become an additional wearable source in Baseline 4PS (it already ingests sleep/HRV/RHR from several brands); a screenless, no-subscription overnight band fits its agency-owned, record-stays-with-you model.
unknowns: No public developer/integration docs found; unclear whether wearables connect directly or via HealthKit/an aggregator; 'and more' list not itemised; no named partnerships contact.
ask: 15-minute call with the Baseline 4PS product lead on how new wearables get added as data sources.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. Baseline 4PS pulling sleep, HRV and resting HR into a record the responder owns is close to what we're building toward: a screenless band worn overnight with an open SDK and no subscription. How do you decide which wearables to support next? I'd value 15 minutes to learn what your agencies ask for.

name: FOP Division of Wellness Services (provider network + State Wellness Liaison Cadre)
why: National FOP created a full-time Division of Wellness Services in 2019; it connects members to vetted wellness practitioners and runs a State Wellness Liaison Cadre with a point of contact in each State Lodge (incl. Ohio). The FOP site hosts provider listings (e.g., Lighthouse Health & Wellness), which is a defined route to officers.
opportunity: Ask how a product gets onto the FOP wellness provider list and be introduced to the Ohio State Lodge wellness liaison for a small officer feedback group.
unknowns: Criteria/cost for provider listing not published; Ohio liaison not named in results; whether consumer hardware vendors are accepted.
ask: Ask the Division of Wellness Services what the provider-listing criteria are and who the Ohio State Lodge wellness liaison is.
opener: Hello, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight band (sleep and HRV, general wellness, no subscription) and want officer feedback before launch. Could you tell me how wellness providers are considered for the FOP listing, and whether the Ohio State Lodge wellness liaison takes this kind of request?

name: Compass Program WHOOP rollout for police and firefighters
org: City of Huntington, WV - Compass first responder wellness program
why: Huntington's Compass program (police and fire wellness center with gym, sauna, coaching, started 2018 with a Bloomberg Mayors Challenge award) equipped officers and firefighters with WHOOP bands to track recovery, sleep, strain and stress, funded by a $20,000 Pallottine Foundation grant. A department already paying for a screenless HRV/sleep band, 10 minutes from the Ohio border.
why_now: WHOOP rollout reported by the Herald-Dispatch (article date not shown in results).
ask: 20-minute call with the Compass coordinator on what worked and didn't with the WHOOP pilot (adherence, data access, cost after year one).
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health, a small team in Akron building a screenless overnight band with an open SDK and no subscription. I read about Compass giving officers and firefighters WHOOP bands. Would you share 20 minutes on what you learned (wear time, who sees the data, renewal cost)? We're trying to build what departments like yours actually need.

name: FireBeats / MyBeats (NYU Tandon fire research)
org: NYU Tandon School of Engineering - FireBeats
why: FireBeats is an AI remote-monitoring app for firefighters that reads personal wearable health trackers to flag cardiovascular risk factors (sudden cardiac events are 50-60% of on-duty deaths per the project). Its App Store sibling MyBeats says it monitors data from 'Fitbit, Garmin, Apple, etc.' - a multi-brand firefighter app that depends on consumer wearables.
opportunity: Offer a DevKit so FireBeats can test an ECG/HRV band worn overnight as a data source; Fitbit Web API sunset pressure makes a new open-SDK source relevant to a Fitbit-dependent research app.
unknowns: Whether FireBeats and MyBeats are the same team/product; how data is pulled (vendor APIs vs HealthKit); no named contact in results; impact of Fitbit API changes on them not confirmed.
ask: Offer one DevKit v0.1 and ask what data format/API their pipeline expects.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. FireBeats reading firefighters' own trackers for cardiac risk factors is a use case we'd like to support. We make a screenless band worn overnight that records ECG and HRV, with a licensed SDK. Would your team want a DevKit to see if it fits your pipeline? Happy to match whatever data format you use.

name: Ohio Office of First Responder Wellness
org: Ohio Department of Public Safety, Office of Criminal Justice Services
why: State office dedicated to the wellbeing of Ohio law enforcement, fire, EMS, dispatch, corrections and Ohio-based military; provides training and support to agencies. Its parent ODPS runs the First Responder Recruitment, Retention and Resilience Program, which has funded agency wellness programs (mental, physical, emotional) across Ohio, so agencies have wellness budgets the office influences. ODPS also hosted a First Responder Family Wellness Day on 2026-10-01 in Columbus.
why_now: ODPS 2026 First Responder Family Wellness Day held 2026-10-01; recurring wellness award rounds (7th round reported).
opportunity: Get Vybe onto the office's radar as an Ohio-made option agencies can pilot under their wellness programs; ask to table at the next ODPS wellness day.
unknowns: Current director (Steven M. Click was named at the 2021 launch; may have changed); whether the office lists or recommends vendors; no vendor route published.
ask: Ask for 15 minutes with the office and whether vendors/resource tables are allowed at the next ODPS wellness event.
opener: Hello, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight band for sleep and HRV (general wellness, no subscription) and want Ohio first responders shaping it before launch. Could we have 15 minutes to learn what agencies in your programs ask for, and whether resource tables are welcome at future ODPS wellness events?

why: Won NLEOMF's 2025 Destination Zero Comprehensive Wellness award: on-duty workout time, on-site gym, group workouts and challenges, free wellness exams, incentives through the Sydney Health app, peer/chaplain programs and annual clinician screening; sick time reportedly halved 2023 to 2024. A small Cuyahoga County department already rewarding tracked wellness goals.
why_now: 2025 Destination Zero Comprehensive Wellness winner (NLEOMF, 2025 awards).

opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health, about 30 minutes south in Akron. Congratulations on the Destination Zero wellness award. We're building a screenless band worn overnight (sleep and HRV, no subscription) and want feedback from departments that already take wellness seriously. Would a few volunteer officers try five bands for 60 days and tell us what's useless?

name: Washington Township Fire Department fitness & wellness program (RFP)

why_now: 2025 RFP published on the township site; submission deadline not shown in results (likely past).

We're building a screenless overnight band (sleep and HRV, general wellness) and want to learn from fire programs. Could you point me to whoever runs the program now? I'd like to offer a test kit for feedback.
